reviews.text: Decentraland is an Ethereum-based metaverse with virtual land NFTs. Launched in 2017, it uses MANA for transactions. In 2025, it hosts events and is governed by a DAO.

Decentraland is a blockchain-based virtual world on Ethereum. Users buy LAND parcels as NFT, and build 3D scenes, play games, and socialize. The entire ecosystem is working on a single currency, the MANA token. The project pioneered the metaverse NFT trend. For example, a single 6100sqft Fashion Street plot sold for $2.4 million (618,000 MANA) in late 2021. It’s governed by a DAO and actively hosts events, like decentraland art week and including crypto conferences and elections. Every person uses an avatar and can interact with people, enter houses and join events. Decentraland, from my perspective, is a virtual reality city owned by its citizens, as the metaverse is decentralized. It was a nice concept during pandemic times, but nowadays the interest is down.

Decentraland is one of the first virtual worlds on blockchain, which is cool. I’ve enjoyed walking around its metaverse events and buying digital land for fun. The idea of a community owned world is impressive. On the other hand, I note how small its real activity is. Reports have shown shockingly low daily user numbers like a few dozen, despite its infrastructure. It also deals with the same issues as crypto its token MANA often lingers rangebound since it’s tied to speculative demand. In short, I think it’s a visionary project but it still struggles to engage mainstream users.
Decentraland is a virtual world built on the blockchain, where users can own land, create experiences, and trade virtual assets using its native token, MANA.
